newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua's gov't, Sandinistas meet over stability.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua's gov't, Sandinistas meet over stability.

text.p: Representatives of Nicaragua's new right-wing government and the opposition Sandinista Front on Monday began a series of meetings to resolve problems with private property and the rule of law.

In a meeting he described as "frank and courteous," the head of the government delegation, Vice President Enrique Bolanos, told a news conference both sides agreed to meet again on Feb. 6 to continue what could be lengthy negotiations.
"The talks we will have with the Sandinista Front will apparently be various. We will iron out the wrinkles in the legal regimen, especially in relation to the property problem," Bolanos said.
At issue is the fate of thousands of properties confiscated by the state under the 1979-1990 revolutionary Sandinista government and now being contested by both their current and former occupants.
A resolution of the property issue is one of the central demands of the business community and foreign investors.

While the government of President Arnoldo Aleman, who took power on Jan. 10, clearly saw the meetings as a victory and a major step toward political stability, the left-wing Sandinistas were less jubilant.

"For us this effort is not to form a pact that will erase our political and ideological differences, but a patriotic effort in search of stability, governability and social peace in benefit of the poorest sectors of society," the head of the Sandinista delegation, Congressman Bayardo Arce, said.

The Sandinistas, still smarting over an Oct. 20 election loss to Aleman they claim was fraudulent, said they were willing to meet the government delegation for Nicaragua's sake but were wary of its intentions.

"We have serious doubts about whether the government is really serious about negotiating and cooperating, and we think beneath it all what they want is to roll back the changes of the (1979 Sandinista) revolution," Sandinista Congressman Victor Hugo Tinoco said.
